description: About 1,080 of the world's larger seaports as named points with a cartographic importance rank. Used in place of the NGA World Port Index (Pub. 150), whose API answered HTTP 503 (maintenance page) when this adapter was built.

coverage.temporal: Static reference data; the port list is revised rarely (Natural Earth 5.x)

updateCadence.upstream: Occasional Natural Earth releases (months to years apart)

attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.

license.name: Public domain (Natural Earth terms of use)
license.notes: "All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data found on this website are in the public domain." No permission or credit is required. The file is fetched from the project's official GitHub repository (nvkelso/natural-earth-vector).

limitations: Substitute dataset: the NGA World Port Index was not reachable, so harbour size and type, maximum vessel size, channel depth, facilities and the country field of that index are NOT available here.
Only a name, a website (often outdated or missing) and Natural Earth's cartographic rank are published per port; the rank reflects map importance, not measured traffic.
A selection of roughly 1,080 larger ports – many commercial ports and all small harbours are absent.
Positions are single points suitable for small-scale maps; the country shown is looked up from the coordinates by this application and can be missing or wrong for ports on a coastline or border.
confidenceNotes: No per-record confidence is published. Volunteer-compiled cartographic reference data; names and positions of major ports are reliable at small scale, attribute detail is minimal.

retention.note: Reference data: a port is kept for as long as the current file lists it.

layers.name: Seaports
layers.description: Larger seaports of the world from Natural Earth (name, website, cartographic importance rank).
